status: G5 final batch: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g5-lusoria, in Chapters I, II, IV, VIII and X (on the web in Chapter II only)
use: A Roman river patrol boat of the Danube fleet afloat on the distant river beyond the board's north edge, in the battles whose scenes have it.

generator.prompt: A Roman river patrol boat of the Danube fleet, a navis lusoria: a long narrow open rowing galley about nine metres long and two metres wide, its low hull of dark tarred oak planks curving up at bow and stern, twelve oars a side resting level on the water line, the mast lowered and laid along the benches with its furled square sail, a broad steering oar at the stern and a row of plain red oval shields along the gunwale. Dark tarred oak, red shields and pale furled linen. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. No environment, ground plane, decorative display plinth, modern materials, text, logos or people.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A long open rowing galley of dark tarred planks with six oars a side, not twelve, round red shields along its gunwale and stem and stern posts curving up to red-capped heads, its mast raised and its square sail set rather than lowered along the benches as asked. Accepted: from the battle's distance it reads as an oared river warship, its pale sail the brightest thing on the river. Processed from its raw proportions at 9.1 m long and 5.7 m to the masthead, 5.4 m across its oars.
